title: Home Internet in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Fewer than half of measured German households get the speed they pay for.** The Bundesnetzagentur's tenth annual report, published 18 June 2026, found **45.9 per cent** of fixed-line users reached their full contracted download rate and **85.9 per cent** got at least half of it.

**Your contract has three speeds, not one.** The Vertragsinformationsblatt lists a **maximum**, a **normally available** and a **minimum** download. Only the maximum is ever advertised, and every legal test below is measured against all three.

**A browser speed test proves nothing.** The evidence a provider has to answer is the Messprotokoll from the Bundesnetzagentur's Breitbandmessung Desktop-App: **10 measurements a day on three different calendar days**, at least one clear day between them, no more than 14 days end to end.

**Any one of three rules is enough.** Missing 90 per cent of the maximum on two of three days, missing the normally available speed in 90 per cent of readings, or dropping under the minimum on two of three days. Hit one and you can **cut the bill in proportion or terminate without notice**.

**Four smaller payments almost nobody claims.** A missed technician appointment is **€10 or 20 per cent** of the monthly charge; a fault unfixed after two days is **€5 or 10 per cent** on days three and four and **€10 or 20 per cent** from day five; a provider switch that leaves you offline more than one working day is **€10 or 20 per cent** per further working day.

**Berlin is about half fibred.** The Senate's figure of 4 March 2026 is **53.4 per cent** of premises passed by fibre against a federal average of 42.9 per cent, but **96.2 per cent** are gigabit-capable once cable is counted. Check your own address on the Bundesnetzagentur's Breitbandatlas.

**The cable fee left your service charges on 1 July 2024.** Since the Nebenkostenprivileg ended, a landlord may not bill a monthly broadband or cable basic fee through the Betriebskostenabrechnung. A new fibre installation fee may be charged, capped at **€60 a year and €540 in total** per flat.
